name: THS4032 (TI dual high-speed low-noise voltage-feedback op-amp)
tagline: 1.6 nV/rtHz, 100 MHz TI video/comms dual that Head-Fi op-amp rollers praise for detail and imaging, despite heat and oscillation risk.
technology: Dual high-speed, ultra-low-voltage-noise voltage-feedback op-amp on TI's 30-V dielectrically isolated complementary bipolar process (NPN/PNP fT of several GHz). Made for communications, imaging and ADC buffering, not for audio.

lineage.notes: SLOS224 was first issued in July 1999 (per mirror listings) and is still in production with a THS4032-EP variant and the THS4032EVM evaluation board. It is a TI in-house THS part, not an acquired Burr-Brown or National design.

reputation.summary: Head-Fi has a dedicated thread on the THS4032, and it comes up across the long-running 'The Opamp thread'. Posters there call it 'highly recommended for audio although it was not designed with audio in mind', 'bright, detailed, clean, well separated', and one says it has 'probably the best imaging' next to the AD797. These are forum impressions from op-amp rolling, not measurements.
sonic_descriptors: strong imaging (per one Head-Fi comparison vs AD797)
typical_uses: Op-amp rolling in DACs and headphone amps (e.g., Beresford TC7520 DAC thread)
I/V and output stages in DIY audio
Designed for: communications, imaging, low-noise ADC buffering
caveats: Runs hot (about 8.5 mA per channel quiescent)
Can oscillate in sockets or poor layouts: 275 MHz unity-gain bandwidth needs tight decoupling
Surface-mount only (SOIC-8 / MSOP PowerPAD), so rolling needs a DIP adapter
Datasheet headline specs changed between revisions (settling 60 ns to 70 ns)
One reviewer found it thin in the mids

revision_history.changes: First release (per search summary of mirror listings).
Earliest revision found on a mirror (alldatasheet). Front page: 100 MHz (G=2), 275 MHz unity-gain, 100 V/us, 60 ns settling, -90 dBc THD at 1 MHz, 1.6 nV/rtHz, 90 mA, 8.5 mA/ch.

Latest known revision (per E2E post). The current front page gives 70 ns settling (was 60 ns in rev C). Which revision made the change is unknown.

A search summary gives the current TI symlink (ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ths4032.pdf) as 'SLOS224L, revised July 2024'. The changes are not shown. This dates the last known revision five months after rev J (February 2024), so rev K falls between February and July 2024 (date not found).

A search summary confirms the header 'SLOS224I – JULY 1999 – REVISED MAY 2018' (probably from the DigiKey HTML datasheet copy). Its front-page text still reads 100 MHz (G=2), 100 V/us, 60 ns settling (0.1%), 90 mA drive, 8.5 mA/ch. The changes are not shown.
A search summary shows the header 'SLOS224J – JULY 1999 – ...', which confirms rev J exists and keeps the July 1999 original-release date. The revised date and changes were not in the summary.

silicon_changes.when: Between SLOS224C (Apr 2000) and the current new-format revision (exact revision unknown)
silicon_changes.identification: None known. No PCN, new-die note or marking change was found; compare the datasheet revision in use.
silicon_changes.summary: There is no evidence of a die change; only the datasheet headline specs moved. The current datasheet and product pages quote 70 ns 0.1% settling, -96 dBc THD at 1 MHz and 1.2 nV/rtHz, where older revisions gave 60 ns settling (confirmed). The older -90 dBc THD and 1.6 nV/rtHz figures are unconfirmed. This looks like re-characterisation rather than new silicon.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: Likely negligible for audio. Settling in the tens of ns is far beyond audio bandwidth.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: pinout and package unchanged; no PCN found; the differences appear to be datasheet-level only
silicon_changes.verification: Search confirmed that the current THS4032 documentation quotes 70 ns settling (0.1%), -96 dBc THD at 1 MHz and 1.2 nV/rtHz, and that older revisions list 60 ns. The older THD and noise values were not confirmed, and no PCN or die-change evidence was found.

counterfeit_notes: No THS4032-specific counterfeit reports were found in this pass. It is a surface-mount-only part often bought pre-mounted on DIP adapters from marketplace sellers, so buy from authorized distributors and check TI markings and date codes.

OPA1612 / LME49720 (modern audio-targeted low-noise duals, editorial suggestion)

revision_chain_notes:
Texas Instruments SLOS224 (THS4031/THS4032; TI is the only vendor, with no second sources or acquirer re-issues). Chain, oldest to newest:
- Original: July 1999, known only as the 'JULY 1999' base date on every later header. No copy of it has been found.
- A and B: missing; no dates or copies.
- C: April 2000, alldatasheet THS4032EVM copy (38 pages). A datasheetarchive SLOS224C listing was added. alldatasheet 28722 and ic37 735153 (38 pages) may also be rev C but do not show it.
- D, E, F: missing; not found in the search index (one query for D/E/F/B returned nothing).
- G: March 2010. No copy has been matched to it.
- H: June 2016. It is quoted by a mirror, but which of RadioLocman or ManualMachine was not stated.
- I: May 2018, confirmed header 'SLOS224I – JULY 1999 – REVISED MAY 2018'; the DigiKey HTML copy is likely.
- J: February 2024 per earlier summaries; header 'SLOS224J – JULY 1999' confirmed.
- K: exists but undated; it must fall between February and July 2024 if the J and L dates are right.
- L: July 2024 (new). This is the current ti.com symlink.
Still missing: dates and copies for the original, A, B, D, E, F and K; the exact copy that holds G; and which revision changed the 0.1% settling time from 60 ns to 70 ns. Note that the search summaries of the current symlink still quote 60 ns, which conflicts with the earlier note of 70 ns.
Separate THS4031-EP/THS4032-EP Enhanced Product datasheet: its literature number (probably SGLSxxx, not confirmed) and revisions are unknown. Copies with no revision shown were added: alldatasheet 463260 and datasheet4u 1488360/1488359.
Archive seeds for Wayback have been added to recover early revisions: focus.ti.com symlinks, www-s.ti.com/sc/ds and ti.com/lit/gpn.
